title: Canonical provider pinning + automated canary health probes for Private VPC IaC
creator: Alex Kim
description: Background: Private VPC customers require predictable Terraform provider and module behavior during upgrades. Recent incidents showed transient drift and provider incompatibilities when rolling provider updates through the on-prem deployment pipelines. Goal: create a canonical pinning policy plus an automated canary upgrade pipeline that runs lightweight health probes after terraform upgrades to detect provider/module breakages before broad rollout. Scope: - Define canonical provider constraint syntax and lockfile usage for all private VPC modules. - Produce an actionable compatibility matrix (module -> provider ranges + validated matrix entries). - Implement an automated 'canary apply' job that upgrades a small staging VPC, runs health probes, and reports gating metrics. - Provide rollback/playbook artifacts and CI gating for downstream deployment pipelines. Out of scope: major refactor of existing terraform modules (separate refactor tickets will be created).
acceptance_criteria: A canonical provider pinning policy document exists and is adopted by all private VPC terraform modules (examples and enforcement rules in CI)
Compatibility matrix CSV generated that maps module versions to provider version ranges and notes for known incompatibilities
CI job 'iac-canary-upgrade' implemented which (a) applies provider/module upgrade to a canary VPC, (b) runs smoke and latency probes, (c) reports pass/fail and telemetry to the console dashboard
Gating thresholds defined: <1% API error rate lift, key SLOs within 2x baseline latency, no state drift detected by drift detector
Rollback playbook documented and tested with at least one simulated rollback in staging
Automated provider lockfile (terraform.lock.hcl) generation and verification step added to module publishing pipeline
implementation_notes: Provider pinning: prefer >= and < style constraints for minor compatibility (e.g., 3.12.0 <= version < 4.0.0) where upstream semver guarantees behavior; use exact pins only where non-semver changes were observed
Add a module-level CI check that fails if terraform.lock.hcl is missing or has uncommitted changes; provide a helper make target 'make regen-lock'
Compatibility matrix will be stored as CSV in the repo: infra/compatibility/provider_matrix.csv with columns: module, module_version, provider, tested_provider_range, test_sha, notes

Canary pipeline: reusable GitHub Actions workflow 'iac-canary-upgrade.yml' that clones module, bumps provider constraints, runs 'terraform init -upgrade', applies to isolated canary workspace, and executes health checks via a lightweight e2e suite

Health probes: - API smoke (token auth/latency) - KV cache warmup check for inference nodes - Node-level GPU readiness and driver sanity - Terraform state sanity check (no partial resources) - DB connectivity and migration verification (if applicable)

Gating instrumentation: emit metrics to console-metrics: iac.canary.apply.status, iac.canary.api_errors, iac.canary.latency_p95, iac.canary.drift_detected; dashboard tile and alert threshold will be created
Rollout model: canary -> staged (10% private clusters) -> broad. Each stage requires successful canary runs and manual/automatic approval based on config
When a provider exhibits incompatibility, document a temporary shim module version and open a follow-up ENG ticket to upstream patch or module change
rollback_plan: If canary fails: immediately revert provider constraints and module pins in the canary workspace via git revert and run terraform apply to return to known-good state
Use stored terraform state snapshot from before canary apply to restore if drift detected
Block downstream rollout pipelines via feature flag until canary green
If rollback requires code changes, tag the faulty module version and publish a patch with exact pins and retry pipeline after sign-off
test_plan: Unit: lint and validate provider constraints using constrained-tf linter in PR checks
Integration: run the canary pipeline in staging with two independent canaries (us-east & eu-west) to catch region-specific provider issues
Chaos: simulate transient failures during canary apply (API throttling, churn of compute nodes) to validate rollback and idempotency
Long-run: schedule nightly canary applies for minor provider updates with extended probe suite to catch slow regressions
Verify observability: ensure metrics show on dashboard and alerting is exercised in test mode
